definition_en: a drawing of an area seen from above, or a diagram that spreads facts over a space
core_image: 桌上摊着一张折痕很深的地图，河流与小山都画在纸上
scene: 桌上摊着一张折痕很深的地图，河流与小山都画在纸上。We followed the map to the park.
sceneCN: 这里 map 是「地图」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们照着地图去了公园。

senses.title: A drawing of an area seen from above
senses.definition: A drawing of an area seen from above
senses.definitionCN: 从上方看到的一片区域的图
senses.example: We followed the map to the park.
senses.exampleCN: 我们照着地图去了公园。
senses.why: Map came from Latin mappa, a cloth, because early maps were painted on cloth; English kept the everyday sense of a paper guide.
senses.whyCN: map 源自拉丁语 mappa（布），早期地图绘在布上，英语保留了纸质向导这一日常义。

senses.title: A diagram showing how something is spread
senses.definition: A diagram showing how something is spread
senses.definitionCN: 显示某事物如何分布的图
senses.example: The weather map shows rain in the north.
senses.why: A map places things in space, so scientists borrowed the word for any diagram that spreads facts across an area.
senses.whyCN: 因为地图把事物摆在空间里，科学家就借它指任何把信息铺在区域上的图。

senses.title: To make a drawing of an area
senses.definition: To make a drawing of an area
senses.example: They mapped the valley last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年夏天绘制了那条山谷的地图。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to map is to do what a map does, put a place onto paper.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：map 就是做地图所做的事，把地方落到纸上。

definition_en: to come together with someone, or to satisfy a need or a standard
core_image: 校门口两个孩子迎面撞见，书包带子晃了一下
scene: 校门口两个孩子迎面撞见，书包带子晃了一下。I met my teacher on the way home.
sceneCN: 这里 meet 是「遇见」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我在回家路上遇到了老师。

senses.title: To come together with someone by chance or by plan
senses.definition: To come together with someone by chance or by plan
senses.example: I met my teacher on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 我在回家路上遇到了老师。
senses.why: Old English metan meant to come upon; a chance meeting and an arranged one share the same picture of two paths crossing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 metan 意为碰见；偶遇与约见都共享两条路交叉的同一画面。

senses.title: To satisfy a need or a standard
senses.definition: To satisfy a need or a standard
senses.example: The school meets the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校符合安全规定。
senses.why: A meeting of two things can also mean a demand and a supply arriving together, so meet took the sense of satisfying.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西相遇也可指需求与供给恰好碰头，于是 meet 有了满足之义。

senses.title: A gathering for sports competitions
senses.definition: A gathering for sports competitions
senses.example: Our school held a sports meet in May.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校五月举办了运动会。
senses.why: In British English a meet is a gathering for sport, a short name for the meeting of competitors.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语中 meet 指运动集会，是参赛者相聚的简称。

definition_en: a device that measures an amount, or to measure something with such a device
core_image: 楼道里一只电表转着小盘，数字一格一格往上走
scene: 楼道里一只电表转着小盘，数字一格一格往上走。The water meter is under the sink.
sceneCN: 这里 meter 是「计量器」（第 01 个义项）；句意是水表在水槽下面。

senses.title: A device that measures an amount
senses.definition: A device that measures an amount
senses.example: The water meter is under the sink.
senses.why: Meter came from Greek metron, a measure; the device that does the measuring took the name directly.
senses.whyCN: meter 源自希腊语 metron（尺度），做测量的装置直接承用了这个名字。

senses.title: To measure something with a device
senses.definition: To measure something with a device
senses.example: The machine meters the gas we use.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器计量我们用的煤气。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to meter is to do what a meter does, record an amount.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：meter 就是做计量器所做的事，记录用量。

senses.title: The basic unit of length in the metric system
senses.definition: The basic unit of length in the metric system
senses.example: The room is four meters long.
senses.why: American spelling meter and British metre both come from Greek metron; the unit keeps the older sense of a measure of length.
senses.whyCN: 美式 meter 与英式 metre 同出希腊语 metron；单位义保留了长度尺度的原义。
